To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Regge states are directly produced at the Lhc and that they can be observed in the processes we considered.
the amplitudes for the production of excited Regge states in string collisions can be expressed in terms of a few universal functions and that they have been evaluated and tabulated.

the production cross sections of the lightest Regge excitations of the open superstring in four dimensions can be expressed as a sum over helicity amplitudes of a massive state and a massless one, and that the amplitudes are given in terms of the corresponding string coupling constants and the masses and momenta of the particles in the final state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of excited Regge states of the lightest string resonances at the LHC.
the study of the production of excited states of the lightest string resonances in the collisions of partons in the context of the Large Hadron Collider.
the study of the production of the lightest Regge resonances, i.e. the first excited level states of open strings, in the collisions of the massless superstring states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the production of the first excited Regge states of light open string excitations is possible in all the above processes and that the production rates are of the same order of magnitude as the corresponding rates for the lowest mass level.

the direct production of lightest Regge excitations at the LHC, as well as the production of the lightest Regge states in electron–positron annihilation, can provide a unique opportunity for a detailed study of the string structure of the Universe.
, in the case of lightest Regge excitations, we have found that the production cross sections are not very large but not very small either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have constructed the covariant vertex operators for the first excited level in the open string spectrum ending on D-brane and have evaluated the partonic cross section for their direct production in the collisions of four-dimensional superstring massless states.
we provide a set of tools for the study of the first excited Regge states of the superstring spectrum, which is a first step towards a full description of the superstring phenomenology at the LHC.

, in the context of lightest Regge resonances, we have completed the construction of covariant vertex operators, have evaluated the amplitudes in the helicity bases, have evaluated partonic cross sections and have tabulated the results in an easy-to-use form.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the production cross sections are typically of the order of a few picobarns, which is a few orders of magnitude higher than the corresponding cross sections for direct production of Kaluza–Klein modes of massive graviton and gravitino.
the Regge states are produced with a cross section comparable to the one of the corresponding massless string states.
the production of excited string states is suppressed relative to the production of the ground-state string by a factor of the inverse of the string mass squared.
